title: NOOB — Agentic SDLC Orchestration Platform

overview.summary: NOOB is an async human-in-the-loop orchestration platform for AI-driven software development. It coordinates stateless AI agents — called Noobs — with human stakeholders across a structured, opinionated software development lifecycle (SDLC). Humans decide; agents mutate; the system records.
overview.problem: AI coding agents are powerful but ungoverned — they operate without structure, auditability, or clear human oversight. Teams either micromanage every step or lose visibility entirely. There is no platform that provides a disciplined, auditable, human-in-the-loop workflow for AI-assisted software development at the team level.
targetAudience: Software product teams using AI agents to build software
Product Owners, Business Analysts, Architects, Developers, QA engineers, and DevOps engineers working in structured SDLC workflows
Engineering leads who need audit trails and governance over AI-generated outputs
Process Refiners who need cross-project analytics to improve pipeline quality
corePrinciples: System owns truth — JSON artefacts, messages, feedback, and validation results are strict, enforced, and auditable
Git supports it — storage, history, diffs; not the domain model
UI drives behaviour — opinionated and structured; no freeform chaos

goals: Provide a structured, stage-gated SDLC workflow that coordinates human stakeholders and AI agents
Ensure every artefact change is traceable to a human decision via a complete audit trail
Prevent ungoverned agent mutations through validation, ownership enforcement, and commit-message coupling
Support asynchronous human review workflows without blocking agent progress unnecessarily
Enable lightweight, fast read-only agent queries (oracle mode) without spinning up compute
Capture telemetry data to surface pipeline health, agent performance, and human engagement quality
Deliver a Phase 1 working system with C# / SQLite backend and React/Vite frontend
nonGoals: Jira integration — explicitly out of scope and not a phase target
Real-time push notifications — deferred to Phase 2
Production deploy automation — NOOB marks as released but does not trigger deploys
Human direct artefact editing — humans express intent via messages only
General-purpose agent framework — NOOB is an opinionated c-SDLC implementation
Analytics view and cross-project metrics — deferred to Phase 2
PDF and binary source file support — text formats only in Phase 1
Real authentication — username-only auth in Phase 1

functionalRequirements.description: The system shall support a fixed stage sequence: Discovery → Clarification → Design → Build → Review → DevOps, with Test Prep running in parallel with Design and Build.
Each project shall have an immutable git slug (auto-generated from display name at creation, user-overridable before confirmation) and a mutable display name.
The docs repo shall be auto-created by NOOB at project creation as a local bare git repo. The code repo shall be connected externally via remote URL and SSH deploy key.
Worker Noobs shall execute in Docker containers. The container receives a brief and feedback as input, writes artefact files, and exits. All validation and business logic runs outside the container.
Oracle mode shall respond to @mention queries via a direct API call with no container, no writes, and access to the docs repo and the named Noob's working-state snapshot.
At the end of every worker run, the Noob shall write a working-state snapshot (currentTask, openQuestions, status, nextLikelyActions) to the database.
All artefacts shall be stored as JSON. Markdown rendering shall be produced on demand and never committed or edited directly.
Every agent commit shall reference a messageId. Commits without a valid message reference shall be rejected.
Artefact names shall follow the convention {type}_{qualifier} (e.g. spec_auth, tasks_payments). Conflict detection shall operate on the fully-qualified name.
Artefacts shall have two lifecycle states: Active (owned by exactly one Noob, writable) and Archived (unowned, read-only). Archiving is a human action.
A Noob's assigned artefact may be reassigned by a human when the Noob is in Waiting or Parked state, accompanied by new feedback scoping the updated task.

All agent output shall be treated as untrusted. Validation shall enforce: schema correctness, referential integrity, file boundary limits (agent may only write to its assigned artefact), stage ownership, and commit identity rules.
Validation results shall be: Pass (commit accepted), Soft Fail (commit accepted with warning, metrics not updated), or Hard Fail (commit rejected, agent must resubmit).
Phase 1 validation scope: spec and tasks artefacts only. PRD, TDS, testcases validation deferred to Phase 2.

The system shall support three explicit interaction types: normal message (human discussion, Noob sees nothing), @mention (oracle query, read-only response), and Send Feedback (worker instruction, may trigger mutation). No auto-routing.
Typing # in any message thread shall open artefact autocomplete, inserting a structured reference that renders as a tappable chip and is stored as artefactRefs on the feedback entity.
Typing $ in any message thread shall open source file autocomplete, inserting a structured reference that renders as a tappable chip and injects the file content into the Noob's execution context.
Send Feedback shall only be enabled when at least one human reply exists in the current cycle. It packages replies into a versioned Feedback entity and dispatches to the worker Noob.
Noobs shall have four states: Working (executing in container), Waiting on humans (message posted), Parked (NFA'd, idle), Dismissed (removed entirely). Dismiss is only available from Parked state.
Noobs that write code shall be assigned a branch in the code repo on first commit: noob/{project-slug}/{noob-name}. PRs and merges are handled by developers outside NOOB.

Humans shall be able to upload source files (text formats only, max 5 MB) at stage or project level. Files are stored in the docs repo under /inputs/{stage}/ or /inputs/project/. Duplicate filenames are rejected.
The Review stage shall only open when Build has reached deployable state AND Test Prep has produced a valid testcases artefact.
The DevOps stage shall surface UAT deploy state, CI/CD pipeline status, release notes generation, and a 'Mark as released to production' human gate action.

The system shall flag message.isStale when a message has had no activity for 48 hours, and stage.isStalled when a stage has been active with no commits for 24 hours. Phase 1: visibility only, no enforcement.

The system shall capture all Easy telemetry fields (per-run records, feedback cycle records, human interaction records, process records) in Phase 1. Schema shall include all Medium and Hard fields as nullable.
# artefact mention structural detection (Option A) shall be implemented at dispatch time. A commit touching files outside the Noob's assigned artefact is always rejected by the validation layer.
The system shall route agent tasks by type: Type A (deep reasoning) to Sonnet, Type B (structured edits) to Haiku, Type C (deterministic validation/diffing) to code-only with no model invocation.

The system shall provide a Message View (primary working view, open messages across projects/stages with filters and staleness sort) and a Stage View (stage strip + drill-down with artefact list, Noobs section, and Hire button).
The Diff View shall be accessible from any message with a registered commit hash, showing both a structural JSON diff and a rendered Markdown diff.

Notifications shall be a distinct entity from messages — FYI only, no reply, no lifecycle. Generated by SOT artefact changes, stuck detection, UAT loop-back events, and pipeline status changes. Data model in Phase 1; display surface deferred to Phase 2.

nonFunctionalRequirements.description: Every artefact mutation shall trace back to a human decision. Every human decision shall trace forward to an artefact change. The audit path is: artefact ↔ commit ↔ feedback ↔ message.
Oracle mode responses shall be designed for conversational response times. Worker runs are async and not expected to be real-time.

The cost strategy shall be: deterministic first (no model) → Haiku for bounded queries → Sonnet for deep reasoning. Avoid unnecessary embedding and retrieval cost — most operations should never touch an LLM.
Agent containers are untrusted producers. All output is treated as untrusted input until validated outside the container. Agents may only write to their assigned artefact.
Phase 1 stack: C# minimal API + SQLite backend, React/Vite frontend, single container, single port, username-only auth.
approvedBy, approvedAt, and stageTransitionReason must be recorded on every stage state change from Phase 1. These fields underpin gate effectiveness and decision quality analysis in later phases.

agentAPI.description: The following Agent API endpoints shall be exposed in Phase 1

endpoints.purpose: Post a message; optionally tag roles
Register commit; triggers validation; returns pass/soft fail/hard fail
Read task state: brief, phase, open messages, latest feedback
Read latest feedback for a thread
Notify SOT file change; triggers cross-stage invalidation

openQuestions.question: PM agent brief intake: text message, file upload, or git repo path?
Generated summaries trigger: on new message, new commit, or both?
UAT loop-back mechanism: new message in Build, or direct task append to tasks artefact? Who creates it — DevOps agent or human?
Oracle response threading: does the oracle response appear as a Noob message in the thread, or as a distinct UI element?
Telemetry push vs derived: does the agent push telemetry via API, or does the system derive it from commit/message timestamps?

Cross-artefact write guard Options B and C: is latency + cost of a pre-dispatch Haiku intent check (B) preferable to container-side intent declaration (C) for handling free-text cross-artefact instructions not caught by # syntax?

phase1.label: Phase 1 — In Scope
items: C# minimal API + SQLite backend; React/Vite frontend; single container; single port; username-only auth
Full Noob lifecycle: Working, Waiting, Parked, Dismissed
All four stages fully implemented: Discovery, Clarification, Design, Build, Test Prep (parallel), Review, DevOps
Two-repo model: docs repo auto-created; code repo externally connected via URL + SSH deploy key
Worker agent execution: Dockerised thin runner; validation outside container
Oracle mode: @mention routes to read-only response
Working-state snapshot: written at end of worker run, read at start of next run
Chat model: normal message / @mention / Send Feedback — explicit, no auto-routing
# artefact mention: autocomplete, chip rendering, artefactRefs on feedback
$ source file mention: autocomplete, chip rendering, content injection into Noob context
Artefact naming convention: {type}_{qualifier} enforced at hire time
Artefact lifecycle: archive, reassignment, pre-creation
Artefact validation: spec and tasks artefacts
Commit ↔ message coupling enforcement
JSON diff + rendered Markdown diff view
Per-artefact concurrency enforcement and cross-artefact write guard (Option A)
Review stage gate: requires Build (deployable) + Test Prep (valid testcases)
Stuck detection: stale message + stalled stage flags (background job; visibility only)
Telemetry recording for all agent actions (data captured; UI Phase 2)
Source files: human-uploaded per stage or project; text formats only; 5 MB limit
Notifications data model (display surface Phase 2)
Project identity: display name + immutable git slug
Role colour coding; dark mode toggle; manual refresh (no real-time push)
Message View and Stage View
Agent API including snapshot and telemetry endpoints
UAT feedback loops; DevOps stage UAT deploy surface, pipeline state, release notes, mark-as-released action

Medium-difficulty telemetry fields active; all derived metrics live; repeat failure detection live
